name: Alabama
notes: ALEA currently lists 50 practice hours, or completion of an approved driver-education course. Some older summaries still say 30 hours.
No separate night-hour minimum is listed. Under-18 applicants generally hold the learner permit for at least six months.

name: Alaska
notes: At least 10 of the 40 hours must involve progressively challenging conditions, such as bad weather or nighttime driving. This is not a night-only quota.
Hold a learner permit for at least six months. Night, poor weather, or a manually marked challenging drive contributes once to the challenging-condition goal; review whether the practice qualifies.

name: Arizona
notes: An eligible traffic-survival or certified defensive-driving-school education route reduces practice to 20 hours, including 6 at night.
A qualifying high-school or private driver-education program is another route. Check ADOT's options before choosing a preset; generally hold the permit for six months.

sources.label: Arizona MVD — Teen Permit and License Requirements

name: Arkansas
notes: No fixed supervised-practice hour minimum is listed in the state guidance; IIHS also lists none. Set personal practice goals rather than treating this as no need to practice.
Age, supervised-driving, driving-record, and graduated-license restrictions still apply.

sources.label: Arkansas DFA — Learner's and Intermediate License

name: California
notes: Practice with an eligible California-licensed adult age 25 or older.
The 50 practice hours are separate from six hours of professional driver training. A permit generally must be held for six months.

name: Colorado
notes: Use the state's DR 2324 log and hold an instruction permit for at least 12 months.
Drivers younger than 16½ have a separate behind-the-wheel training requirement; qualifying distance/hardship alternatives have additional conditions.

sources.label: Colorado DMV — Drive Time Log, DR 2324

name: Connecticut
notes: The 40 practice hours may combine qualified parent, commercial-school, and secondary-school instruction. No separate night-hour minimum is listed.
The permit wait is generally 120 days for the qualifying school-training route or 180 days for home training. Safe-driving and parent-training requirements also apply.

name: Delaware
notes: A sponsor certifies the practice during the first six months, before unsupervised driving.
The full Level One program lasts 12 months; approved driver education and sponsor requirements also apply.

name: District of Columbia
appliesTo: Learner stage of the GRAD program
notes: The learner stage requires 40 supervised hours. A separate 10-hour supervised-night certification comes during the provisional stage, before the full license with conditions.
Do not combine these stages into a single 40-total/10-night preset. Stage-specific certification and eligibility rules apply.

alternativePresets.label: Provisional to full — new nighttime practice

name: Florida
notes: A parent, guardian, or other responsible adult certifies the practice; the permit is generally held for 12 months or until age 18.
Learners initially drive only in daylight, then may drive until 10 p.m. after three months. Check current education and eligibility requirements.

sources.label: Florida FLHSMV — Certification of Driving Experience

name: Georgia
notes: Joshua's Law has different school and parent-taught training methods. Complete the requirements for the chosen method as well as the supervised practice.
Do not automatically add school-training time twice when using the parent-taught route.

name: Hawaii
notes: State public-school guidance calls for 40 daytime hours and 10 nighttime hours with a licensed adult age 21 or older.
Driver education and a notarized practice acknowledgement/log are required by the program. Check the instructor and county licensing office.

sources.label: Hawaii DOE — Molokai High School Driver Education

name: Idaho
notes: Complete the required driver-training program, then the supervised instruction period of at least six months.
State education guidance specifies 40 daytime and 10 nighttime hours; the preset keeps these as separate goals.

sources.label: Idaho Department of Education — Driver Education

name: Illinois
notes: Practice is supervised by an eligible parent or licensed adult age 21 or older.
Hold the instruction permit for at least nine months and meet the driver-education requirements. Permit curfews and passenger restrictions also apply.

sources.label: Illinois Secretary of State — Graduated Driver's License

name: Indiana
notes: Use the BMV supervised-driving log and an eligible supervising driver; eligibility varies by age.
A daylight-only permit restriction exempts the night portion, but not the 50-hour total. Driver-education and permit-holding rules are separate.

name: Iowa
notes: The night portion is practice after sunset. Approved driver education is a separate requirement.
Iowa has additional stages and special minor licenses. Check the applicable stage; do not treat an intermediate-license goal as the entire path to a full license.

sources.label: Iowa DOT — Parent's Supervised Driving Program

name: Kansas
notes: The age-15 restricted route starts with at least 25 supervised hours; the 50-hour affidavit is needed to advance to less restricted privileges.
Practice is supervised by an eligible licensed adult age 21 or older. Age, farm-permit, driver-education, and permit-duration rules affect the route.

name: Kentucky
notes: Practice with a licensed driver age 21 or older in the front passenger seat.
Before advancing, hold the permit at least 180 days, reach age 16, and have a parent/guardian certify the practice log.

name: Louisiana
notes: Practice with a licensed parent, guardian, or adult age 21 or older.
The intermediate-license route has separate age, permit-holding, education, and testing requirements.

sources.label: Louisiana OMV — Class E Intermediate License

name: Maine
notes: Log practice after the learner permit is issued; the night portion is after dark.
Hold the permit at least six months. Under-18 applicants also need approved driver education; supervising-driver and certification requirements apply.

name: Maryland
notes: These are supervised practice hours, separate from the required driver-education program.
Age changes the permit-holding rules; applicants age 25 or older have a different practice requirement. Check the MVA age-specific route.

name: Massachusetts
notes: Practice is additional to driver education. A qualifying driver-skills development program can reduce supervised practice to 30 hours.
No separate night-hour quota is listed. Education includes separate classroom, driving, and observation requirements.

name: Michigan
notes: The practice log must be complete before the driving-skills test.
Segment 1 and Segment 2 driver education and Level 1 holding requirements also apply; earlier training milestones are not a substitute for the full 50-hour log.

name: Minnesota
notes: If a parent/guardian completes the approved 90-minute parent-awareness class, the total drops to 40 hours; the 15 nighttime hours remain.
Complete the required driver education and submit the supervised-driving log.

name: Mississippi
notes: No fixed supervised-practice hour minimum is listed in the licensing guidance; IIHS also lists none. The mentor guide's suggested practice schedule is not a statutory hour quota.
Permit, age, parental certification, and driving restrictions still apply. Keep personal practice goals.

name: Missouri
notes: Night practice is between sunset and sunrise. An eligible adult certifies the supervised instruction.
The permit wait is at least 182 days, beginning the day after issuance. Check age-specific supervisor qualifications.

sources.label: Missouri DOR — Graduated Driver License Law

name: Montana
notes: Log supervised practice with an eligible adult and hold the learner license at least six months plus one day.
Driver-training, driving-record, and first-year restrictions also apply.

name: Nebraska
notes: A DMV-approved driver safety course is an alternative to the 50-hour certification route.
For the practice route, night hours are between sunset and sunrise. An eligible parent, guardian, or licensed adult age 21 or older signs the certification.

name: Nevada
notes: The limited education exemption requires 100 practice hours, including 10 at night: no classroom course within 30 miles and no internet access.
Practice with a licensed adult age 21 or older with at least one year of driving experience.

sources.label: Nevada DMV — Driver Education for Teens

name: New Hampshire
notes: These practice hours are additional to the driver-education course.
New Hampshire does not issue a standard passenger-car learner permit. Check the manual for minimum practice age, eligible supervisors, and youth-operator restrictions.

name: New Jersey
notes: The requirement applies to special learner and examination permits issued on or after February 1, 2025; 10 hours must be during darkness.
Earlier permits follow the prior rules. Certification, supervised-period, age, and probationary-license requirements remain separate.

name: New Mexico
notes: Complete the applicable approved driver-education program and generally hold an instruction permit at least six months.
A documented nighttime-vision condition may qualify for a night-driving exemption; check MVD requirements.

sources.label: New Mexico MVD — Provisional Driver's License

name: New York
notes: The nighttime requirement is driving after sunset. A parent/guardian signs form MV-262.
Pre-licensing/driver-education requirements also apply. Supervision and permitted driving vary among New York City, Long Island, and the rest of the state.

name: North Carolina
appliesTo: Level 1 learner to Level 2 limited provisional
notes: The Level 1 log is separate from the later Level 2 practice: an additional 12 hours, including 6 at night, is needed for Level 3.

Level 2 generally requires nine months with the learner permit. Choose the correct stage and its start date. State-specific weekly limits and required forms must still be checked separately; the app does not enforce weekly caps.

sources.label: North Carolina DMV — Supervised Driving Guide

name: North Dakota
notes: Complete 50 hours in varied driving conditions; no separate numerical night quota is listed.
The age-14/15 route also requires a year with the permit and approved driver education. Ages 16–17 have different requirements.

sources.label: North Dakota DOT — Learner Permit and Age-Based Requirements

name: Ohio
notes: The practice hours are in addition to driver education, including its separate classroom and behind-the-wheel instruction.
Permit-holding, eligible-supervisor, certification, and road-test requirements also apply.

name: Oklahoma
notes: The supervising driver must be at least 21 and licensed for at least two years.
Use the driver-training affidavit and meet the separate learner-permit and conviction-free periods.

name: Oregon
appliesTo: Under-18 license, without approved driver education
notes: Passing an ODOT-approved driver-education course reduces supervised practice to 50 hours. No separate numerical night minimum is listed.
The supervising driver must have at least three years of licensed experience for practice to count. Keep a personal night goal.

name: Pennsylvania
notes: The 65-hour total must also include at least 5 hours in poor weather. This is an additional condition, not an extra 5 hours on top of 65.
Hold the learner permit at least six months. Tag qualifying poor-weather practice and review it with the supervising adult.

sources.label: Pennsylvania PennDOT — Get a Driver's License

name: Rhode Island
notes: The night portion is after sunset. A parent/guardian certifies practice with a supervising driver.
Hold the limited instruction permit at least six months and complete the education and road-test requirements.

sources.label: Rhode Island DMV — New License Permits

name: South Carolina
appliesTo: Conditional or special restricted teen license
notes: Practice with a qualified licensed supervisor and complete the required driver education.
Age, permit-holding, school-attendance, and driving restrictions affect which license is available.

name: South Dakota
notes: The 50-hour total also includes 10 hours in inclement weather; a parent/guardian signs the supervised-driving statement.
Permit-holding periods depend on driver education. Tag qualifying inclement-weather practice and review it with the supervising adult.

name: Tennessee
notes: Reach age 16, hold the learner permit at least 180 days, and satisfy driving-record requirements.
A parent, guardian, or driving instructor signs the 50-hour certification.

name: Texas
notes: Only one practice hour per day counts toward this 30-hour requirement. The preset credits the first 60 recorded minutes each calendar day in your saved time zone; additional driving remains in the log.
The 30 hours are separate from the course's seven driving and seven observation hours. Education, permit-holding, and Impact Texas Teen Drivers requirements also apply.

sources.label: Texas DPS — Provisional License as a Teen

name: Utah
notes: The night portion is driving after sunset.
Driver education, permit-holding, parental responsibility, and age-specific supervision requirements also apply.

name: Vermont
notes: These hours are additional to driver education.
For this requirement, night runs from 30 minutes after sunset until 30 minutes before sunrise. Check permit-holding and certification requirements.

name: Virginia
notes: The night portion is driving after sunset and is certified on the driver-education completion certificate.
Hold the learner permit at least nine months and complete a Virginia-approved driver-education program.

name: Washington
notes: Washington specifically requires 40 daylight hours plus 10 nighttime hours, supervised by someone licensed for at least three years.
The preset keeps daylight and nighttime goals separate. Driver training and at least six months with a learner permit also apply.

name: West Virginia
notes: A completed driver-education card is an alternative to the certified 50-hour practice form.
Separate age, permit-holding, driving-record, and road-skills-test requirements apply.

sources.label: West Virginia DMV — Graduated Licensing Brochure

name: Wisconsin
notes: The current standard is 50 hours, including 10 at night. Permits issued before July 11, 2021 had a different total.
Approved driver education, at least six months with an instruction permit, and violation-free requirements also apply.

name: Wyoming
notes: Provide certification of 50 actual behind-the-wheel hours, including 10 at night.
Meet the separate age, learner-permit, parental-consent, and road-test requirements. Restricted hardship permits are a different route.

sources.label: Wyoming DOT — Learner and Intermediate Permits
